title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's notes on the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli multiplicities (orbifolds/stacks) M_{g,ν}. An MD-graph G is a stable dual graph. M_G is the open boundary stratum of curves with dual graph G, taken as an analytic multiplicity, i.e. with its automorphism group Γ_G. \hat M_G is the corresponding closed object.

Previous page. G' = G/C is obtained by contracting a set C of edges, so G' is a less degenerate type and the stratum M_G lies in the closure of M_{G'}. Γ^!_{G,G'} ⊂ Γ_G is the subgroup that stabilizes C and acts trivially on G'. The map (M_G, Γ^!_{G,G'}) → \hat M_{G'} is a (local) immersion. M_{G,G'} and \hat M_{G,G'} denote the germ of the ambient multiplicity along this locally closed sub-multiplicity, in modern terms a tubular neighbourhood of the stratum M_G inside \bar M_{G'}.

This page.
(i) Define \hat M^*_{G,G'} and \hat{\hat M}^*_{G,G'}. These are the germs obtained by removing from these germs the traces of the divisors at infinity, i.e. the boundary divisors meeting the germ. The result is the deleted (punctured) tubular neighbourhood of the stratum, lying in the open part M_{G'}.
(ii) Their fundamental groupoids Π M^*_{G,G'} (eq. 100) are defined as 2-colimits over the system of neighbourhoods of the categories of (universal) coverings. Equivalently they are the covering categories of the germs, viewed as pro-objects. He cross-refers to an earlier text (§53, n°5, p. 768').
(iii) Diagram (101): M^*_{G,G'} → M_{G'} is the inclusion of the deleted neighbourhood into the open stratum. M^*_{G,G'} → M_{G,G'} is the inclusion into the full germ. The full germ is homotopy equivalent to the stratum (M_G, Γ^!_{G,G'}); the 'équivalence d'homotopie !' is the retraction of the tubular neighbourhood onto the stratum.

Next page. Applying Π gives the 'specialization diagram for fundamental groupoids' (102)-(103). One arrow is Π M^*_{G,G'} → Π M_{G'}. The other, φ_{G,G'}, goes to Π(M_G, Γ^!) ≅ Π M_{G,G'}. Since the deleted neighbourhood fibres over M_G with fibre a product of punctured discs indexed by C, Π M^*_{G,G'} is a canonical extension of Π(M_G, Γ^!) by Z^C (Dehn twists around the vanishing cycles). This uses that M_G is a K(π,1).

In modern terms: for a multicurve σ with |σ| = |C|, the stabilizer of σ in the mapping class group of type G' fits in 1 → Z^σ → Stab(σ) → Mod(S∖σ)-type group → 1, and Stab(σ) maps into Γ_{G'}. This is the local, boundary-stratum description of 'tangential base points at infinity' used in the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse.

Purpose: to set up the combinatorics/groupoid data at infinity (specialization maps between fundamental groupoids of strata) needed to describe the 'tour de Teichmüller' and the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on it.
errors: The deleted neighbourhood M^*_{G,G'} is not itself homotopy equivalent to M_{G,G'}. Only the full germ retracts onto (M_G, Γ^!). The parenthetical '(équivalence d'homotopie !)' must be read as referring to (M_G, Γ^!) → M_{G,G'}, not to the vertical arrow from M^*. The left-hand term written M_{G'} in the parenthesis of (101) is presumably a slip for M_G (with Γ^!).

The fibre of M^*_{G,G'} → M_G is a product of punctured discs only up to the finite group Γ^!_{G,G'} and to orbifold structure. The 'extension by Z^C' is therefore an extension of groupoids in the stacky sense; this is not spelled out.

Defining Π of a germ as a colimit of covering categories is fine, but it implicitly needs local analytic triviality (normal crossings of the DM boundary) for the pro-system to be essentially constant. This holds, but is not stated.

ideas.what: Deleted tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum of \bar M_{g,n} (germ minus boundary divisors) and its fundamental groupoid defined via germs of coverings
ideas.modern_name: punctured tubular neighbourhood / link of a stratum; local fundamental group at infinity; 'tangential base points' for higher codimension strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura; Nakamura; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Boggi (profinite Teichmüller theory)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, 'points base à l'infini') at a programmatic level only

ideas.what: Specialization diagram Π M^*_{G,G'} → Π M_{G'} and Π M^*_{G,G'} → Π(M_G, Γ^!), with the first group an extension of the stratum group by Z^C
ideas.modern_name: multicurve stabilizer exact sequence 1→Z^σ→Stab(σ)→Mod(S∖σ)→1 and inertia at boundary strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman–Lubotzky–McCarthy (stabilizers of multicurves); Ihara–Nakamura / Boggi in the arithmetic setting

ideas.what: Retraction of a tubular neighbourhood germ onto the stratum (homotopy equivalence)
ideas.modern_name: tubular neighbourhood theorem for stratified orbifolds

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates, for every edge contraction G → G' = G/C of stable graphs, a specialization diagram of fundamental groupoids of analytic multiplicities attached to deleted neighbourhoods of strata. This is a systematic higher-codimension version of tangential base points, predating the published treatments (Ihara–Nakamura, Boggi, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps). The content is now standard, but this documents his priority-level detailed formulation.
missed.quote: les groupoïdes fondamentaux Π M^*_{G,G'} ... sont définis comme des catégories lim des catégories de revêtements universels ... (équivalence d'homotopie !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows the boundary-groupoid formalism behind the Esquisse Teichmüller tower was worked out stratum by stratum in Grothendieck's notes. Mathematically it is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, explicit early formulation of local fundamental groupoids at boundary strata and the specialization maps for all edge contractions. The mathematics, however, is now standard (multicurve stabilizers, tangential base points, profinite Teichmüller theory), and the page is a definitional set-up rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'germes de multiplicités obtenus en enlevant les traces des diviseurs à l'infini', not 'groupoïdes de multiplicités'.
'On a donc des diagrammes de groupoïdes de multiplicités analytiques' is more plausibly 'diagrammes de germes de multiplicités analytiques'.
The two objects in (100) differ by decoration (Π \hat M^* vs Π \hat{\hat M}^*, or by underlining). The transcription repeats the same symbol.
In (101) the bottom-left term looks like (M_G, Γ^!) → M_{G,G'}, not M_{G'}.
'dits les filtres d'incidence' is uncertain; the reading is unclear in the image.
